title: Numerals 9: Irregular Numerals (полтора, оба/обе, год → лет)
titleRussian: Числительные 9: неправильные числительные (полтора, оба/обе, год → лет)
description: The low-numeral irregulars you have to produce: год/года/лет, полтора/полторы (with the single non-nominative полутора), and the full declension of оба/обе with its gender split.
descriptionRussian: Неправильные формы у небольших числительных, которые нужно уметь образовывать: год/года/лет, полтора/полторы (и единственная косвенная форма полутора) и полное склонение оба/обе с делением по роду.
intro: Three oddities that do not fit the system. One and a half takes the small-number form but collapses to a single genderless shape the moment it leaves the nominative. The word for 'both' does the opposite and keeps its gender split all the way through. And the plural of 'year' remains a word from a different root.
rules: The genitive plural of год is лет (a frozen old form). Use it whenever the number rule asks for the genitive plural: пять лет, много лет, сколько лет. The nominative год and genitive singular года stay regular: один год, два года, пять лет.
Полтора (masculine/neuter) and полторы (feminine) mean 'one and a half' and take the genitive singular: полтора часа, полторы минуты. There is no полтора годов.
In any case other than the nominative, полтора and полторы both become the single form полутора, with no gender split: о полутора часах, к полутора годам.
Оба (masculine/neuter) and обе (feminine) have a full declension and keep the gender split in every case. Masc/neut: оба, обоих, обоим, обоими. Fem: обе, обеих, обеим, обеими.
Choose оба/обе by the noun's gender, then put it in the case its role demands: с обоими братьями (instrumental), у обеих сестёр (genitive), к обоим окнам (dative).
examples: Маше пять лет. (Masha is five years old.) Genitive plural of год = лет.
Я живу здесь много лет. (I have lived here for many years.) Много governs the genitive plural лет, not годов.
Урок длится полтора часа. (The lesson lasts an hour and a half.) Полтора + genitive singular часа.
Антон ждал полторы минуты. (Anton waited a minute and a half.) Feminine полторы + genitive singular минуты.
Лекция шла около полутора часов. (The lecture lasted about an hour and a half.) Non-nominative полутора after около.
У обеих сестёр одинаковые глаза. (Both sisters have the same eyes.) Genitive plural after у; обеих with the stem extension.
Антон гуляет с обоими братьями. (Anton is walking with both brothers.) Instrumental обоими + instrumental plural братьями.
Маша рассказала о сорока студентах. (Masha told us about forty students.) Сорока, the single non-nom-acc form, + prepositional plural.
К девяноста годам он уже забыл многое. (By the age of ninety he had already forgotten a lot.) Dative девяноста (the only non-nominative form) + dative plural годам.
Это книга о ста городах. (This is a book about a hundred cities.) Prepositional ста + prepositional plural городах.
В классе тысяча книг. (There are a thousand books in the classroom.) Тысяча acts as a noun and pulls the genitive plural книг.
Город насчитывает миллион жителей. (The city has a million inhabitants.) Миллион acts as a noun and pulls the genitive plural жителей.

items.promptEnglish: Masha is already five years old.
items.hint: After 5 and up, the genitive plural of год is not годов.
items.explanation: The genitive plural of год is the frozen form лет (from the old word лето). It appears whenever the number rule asks for the genitive plural: пять лет, шесть лет, много лет. Годов does not exist in standard Russian. Года is the genitive singular (два года), and год is the bare nominative (один год).

items.promptEnglish: The lesson lasts an hour and a half.
items.hint: Полтора is built like два. What case does it demand?
items.explanation: Полтора (masc / neut) and полторы (feminine) both take the genitive singular, just like два / две, три, and четыре. Час is masculine, so: полтора часа. Часов is genitive plural and only fits after 5 and up.

items.promptEnglish: Anton is walking with both brothers.
items.hint: С + instrumental. What is the instrumental of оба?
items.explanation: С meaning 'together with' takes the instrumental, and the instrumental of оба is обоими. The masculine form is preserved even in the non-nominative forms: с обоими братьями. The corresponding feminine form would be с обеими сёстрами.

items.promptEnglish: Masha told us about forty students.
items.hint: Сорок has only two case forms. Which one fits after о?
items.explanation: Сорок has exactly two shapes: the nominative-accusative сорок and a single non-nominative form сорока used for every other case. So о (prepositional), к (dative), с (instrumental), and after a verb that wants genitive all take сорока: о сорока студентах. There is no сорокам or сороками in modern Russian.

items.prompt: К _____ годам он уже многое забыл.
items.promptEnglish: By ninety years old he had already forgotten a lot.
items.hint: К + dative. Девяносто has only two forms.
items.explanation: Девяносто works like сорок and сто: two forms total. The nominative-accusative is девяносто; everything else is девяноста. After к (dative): к девяноста годам. The noun also moves to the dative plural годам.

items.promptEnglish: Our city has a million inhabitants.
items.hint: Миллион behaves like a noun and stands in the nominative as the subject.
items.explanation: Миллион is a noun-like numeral. As the subject 'A million inhabitants are in our city,' it stands in the nominative singular миллион. The following noun жителей goes into the genitive plural because миллион (and тысяча) always force the genitive plural on the noun that follows.

blanks: У _____ сестёр одинаковые глаза. (Both sisters have the same eyes.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: У governs the genitive. Сестёр is feminine, so we need the feminine form of 'both' in the genitive: обеих. The masculine / neuter would be обоих, the feminine instrumental would be обеими. The gender split is preserved in every case of оба / обе.

minimalPairs.explanation: Восемнадцать is in the 5-and-up family, so the next noun is the genitive plural of год. The standard genitive plural is the frozen form лет; годов does not exist in modern Russian.

Друзья is masculine, so 'both' is in the masculine form. С + instrumental gives обоими. Обеими would be the feminine instrumental (с обеими подругами). The masculine / feminine split is preserved across every case of оба / обе.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha is already seven years old.
errorCorrection.explanation: The genitive plural of год is the frozen old form лет, used whenever the number rule calls for the genitive plural: семь лет, много лет, сколько лет. Годов is the regular-looking form a learner builds with -ов, but it does not exist in modern Russian. Года is the genitive singular (два года), and год is the bare nominative (один год). Age is given with the dative person: Маше.

errorCorrection.sentence: В этой библиотеке больше стам книг.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This library has more than a hundred books.
errorCorrection.explanation: Сто (like сорок and девяносто) has only two case forms: the nominative-accusative сто and a single non-nominative form ста for every other case. Больше governs the genitive, so the form is ста: больше ста книг. Стам and стах are invented plural-style forms.

errorCorrection.sentence: У обоих сестёр были одинаковые глаза.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Both sisters had the same eyes.
errorCorrection.explanation: The gender split of оба/обе survives in every case. Сёстры is feminine, so 'both' must be feminine throughout, and у takes the genitive: у обеих сестёр. Обоих is the masculine/neuter genitive (у обоих братьев), обеими is the feminine instrumental (с обеими сёстрами), and обе is the feminine nominative (обе сестры). Pick the gender from the noun first, then the case from the role.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The trip took a week and a half.
errorCorrection.explanation: Полтора splits by gender like два/две: полтора for masculine and neuter, полторы for feminine. Неделя is feminine, so the form is полторы недели, with the noun in the genitive singular. Полтора would be right with a masculine or neuter noun (полтора часа). Полутора is the single non-nominative form (к полутора неделям), and полуторы is not a real form.

errorCorrection.sentence: К полтора годам ребёнок начинает ходить.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: By a year and a half a child starts to walk.
errorCorrection.explanation: In any case other than the nominative, полтора and полторы collapse into the single form полутора, with no gender split. К takes the dative, so: к полутора годам. Полтора is the masculine nominative form (полтора года) and полторы the feminine (полторы недели); neither can stand after к. Полуторам adds a regular dative ending that полутора never takes.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: There were a thousand spectators in the stadium.
errorCorrection.explanation: Тысяча behaves like a noun, and like the quantity words 5 and up it forces the following noun into the genitive plural, even when тысяча itself is the nominative subject: тысяча зрителей. Зритель is the nominative singular, the trap of leaving the noun unchanged. Зрителя is the genitive singular (after 2-4: два зрителя). The verb agrees with тысяча, hence the feminine singular была, not были.

patternRecognition.question: Why is the form лет, not годов?
options: лет is the frozen genitive plural of год
лет is the genitive singular of год
лет is the nominative plural of год
лет is a separate word unrelated to год
patternRecognition.answer: лет is the frozen genitive plural of год
patternRecognition.explanation: Сколько asks for the genitive plural, and the genitive plural of год is the frozen form лет (from the old word лето). Годов does not exist in modern Russian.

patternRecognition.question: Why does полтора appear as полутора here?
options: It is the non-nominative form, used in every case but the nominative
It is a spelling error for полторы
patternRecognition.answer: It is the non-nominative form, used in every case but the nominative
patternRecognition.explanation: Около governs the genitive, a case other than the nominative. There полтора and полторы both become the single form полутора, with no gender split: около полутора часов.

patternRecognition.question: Why is the form обоим (masc/neut) and not обеим (fem)?
options: Окно is neuter, so 'both' is the masc/neut form оба → обоим
к always takes обоим regardless of gender
Окно is feminine, so обоим is wrong
patternRecognition.answer: Окно is neuter, so 'both' is the masc/neut form оба → обоим
patternRecognition.explanation: Choose the gender from the noun: окно is neuter, so 'both' is оба. К takes the dative, giving обоим: к обоим окнам. The feminine dative would be к обеим дверям.

reviewVocab.definition: year / of a year / years (gen pl). The genitive plural is the frozen form лет, used after 5+, много, сколько, несколько.
reviewVocab.example: Один год, два года, пять лет, много лет.

reviewVocab.definition: one and a half. Masc/neut полтора, feminine полторы, both + genitive singular. In every case but the nominative both genders collapse to полутора.
reviewVocab.example: Полтора часа, полторы минуты, о полутора часах.

reviewVocab.definition: both. Masc/neut оба (обоих, обоим, обоими); feminine обе (обеих, обеим, обеими). The gender split survives in every case.
reviewVocab.example: С обоими братьями, у обеих сестёр, к обоим окнам.

reviewVocab.definition: forty / ninety / one hundred. Only two case forms each: nom-acc сорок / девяносто / сто, and a single non-nominative form сорока / девяноста / ста covering all other cases.
reviewVocab.example: К девяноста годам, о ста городах.

reviewVocab.definition: thousand / million. Behave as feminine / masculine nouns: full noun declension, and they always force the genitive plural on the next noun.
reviewVocab.example: Тысяча рублей, миллион книг, в тысяче километров.
